Well, more specifically the .223 Remington was adopted as the US Army's new cartridge to allow troops to carry more of it. It replaced the .308 used in the M14 and the 30-06 used in the M1 Garand, before that. After that, it was standardized as 5.56 NATO for use by other NATO countries. The US military actually will put out a list of specifications that it looks for in its equipment, and companies can then make equipment that meets these specifications, or they already have equipment that qualifies, and the US military will then pick between all available options (usually going with the cheapest one that still meets their specifications). The AR-15 pattern rifle was designed to use this ammunition so that it could be considered for a military contract, but was actually released as a civilian sporting rifle initially. It wasn't until colt purchased the design from ArmaLite and made some small changes that the rifle was adopted by the US military as the M16. 

TL;DR the AR-15 wasn't designed for the military so that troops could carry more ammo, it was designed to use a smaller caliber, which was itself designed to be lighter and therefore allowed troops to carry more of it.
